endowment_summary: Began fencing at 13 after initially playing handball and track, switching relatively late. Showed strong athletic capability but not prodigy-level early achievement, rising through Romania's state sports system.
inherited_summary: Born in Bucharest as the youngest of four children. No evidence of family wealth or domain-specific advantages; family background was ordinary.
ecosystem_summary: Trained under coaches Rodica Popescu and Maria Vicol at CSS 1 Bucharest, then joined CSA Steaua București, the Romanian army's elite sports club. Romania's state-funded fencing pipeline provided world-class coaching and competition access.

endowment_summary: Excellent swimmer by age 10, set world records in 1950-51, and won Olympic gold at 22. Demonstrated exceptional early aquatic ability and competitive trajectory from childhood.
inherited_summary: Grew up in Budapest in a swimming family; older sister Ilona was also an elite Olympic swimmer and training partner, providing direct domain exposure and sibling competition.
ecosystem_summary: Joined Ferencvárosi TC, part of the dominant Hungarian women's swimming program of the era. Budapest's swimming infrastructure and national team system provided elite coaching and competition.

endowment_summary: Started basketball at 15 but reached #1 NBA draft pick within 6 years, demonstrating exceptional physical aptitude and rapid learning. Soccer goalkeeper background gave him elite footwork that defined his game.
inherited_summary: Born to Salim and Abike Olajuwon, working-class Yoruba owners of a cement business in Lagos. Third of eight children in a middle-class Nigerian household with no basketball connections.
ecosystem_summary: Recruited to University of Houston by coach Guy Lewis based on a recommendation, joining a program with three consecutive Final Four appearances. Paired with Ralph Sampson in the 'Twin Towers' duo, providing an elite collegiate platform.

endowment_summary: Started handball at 14 and became a first-league goalkeeper before 18, an unusually early debut. Showed strong capability but not prodigy-level dominance in early years.
inherited_summary: No evidence of family wealth or domain-specific advantages. Grew up in Derventa, Bosnia, with no documented family handball background.
ecosystem_summary: Joined Borac Banja Luka, one of Yugoslavia's top handball clubs, at 19. Yugoslavia was a global handball superpower, providing elite competition, coaching, and the national team pipeline.

endowment_summary: Joined Metaloplastika at 20 and became part of a legendary squad. Showed strong goalkeeping ability but was not a standout prodigy in his early teens.
inherited_summary: No evidence of family wealth or domain-specific advantages. Began career with Sloga Hrtkovci and Crvenka before joining Metaloplastika.
ecosystem_summary: Metaloplastika was one of Europe's premier handball clubs in the 1980s, winning consecutive European Cups. Surrounded by elite teammates including Veselin Vujović within the Yugoslav handball powerhouse system.

endowment_summary: Reached Junior French Open final at 18 and won first ATP title at 19, named ATP Newcomer of the Year. Demonstrated exceptional early tennis ability with rapid professional trajectory.
inherited_summary: Father Eduardo introduced him to tennis at 7 and placed him with an elite coach at 9. Middle-class Spanish family; mother Rosario died when he was young, which became a motivational force.
ecosystem_summary: Trained at Antonio Martínez Cascales' academy in Villena from age 9, with Cascales as lifelong coach. Spain was a clay-court tennis powerhouse, providing a strong developmental ecosystem and peer group.

endowment_summary: Started gymnastics at 8 and progressed through Romania's elite pipeline, winning Balkan all-around at 15 and Olympic team gold at 17. Capable but not a standout prodigy in a system full of talented gymnasts.
inherited_summary: No evidence of family wealth or domain-specific advantages. Entered the Romanian gymnastics pipeline through CSȘ Sibiu.
ecosystem_summary: Trained at the Romanian national team center in Deva from age 13, under elite coaches Octavian Bellu and Adrian Goreac. Romania was a world-dominant gymnastics power, providing once-in-a-generation coaching and infrastructure.

endowment_summary: Debuted in Paraguayan first division at 15, an exceptionally early entry showing raw talent. Won league championship at 19. Demonstrated unusual early ability despite harsh conditions.
inherited_summary: Grew up in a poor family in Luque, walked barefoot until age 7. Father was a state bureaucrat; family had limited resources. Had to walk 7km to training and sell milk as a child.
ecosystem_summary: South American football culture provided a strong developmental environment. Trained by Modesto Sandoval at Sportivo Luqueño, a local club. Limited infrastructure but deep football culture in Paraguay.

endowment_summary: Amassed 131 points in junior hockey and was drafted 6th overall at 19. Exceptional skating ability recognized early, progressing rapidly through the OHA junior system.
inherited_summary: Grew up in a working-class family in Malton, Ontario. Father was a bread-delivery driver who made every effort to support his hockey career despite limited means.
ecosystem_summary: Joined the Edmonton Oilers dynasty alongside Wayne Gretzky, Jari Kurri, and Mark Messier — a once-in-a-generation peer environment. The OHA junior hockey pipeline (North York Rangers, Sault Ste. Marie, Kitchener) provided elite development.

endowment_summary: Joined Cuban national team at 18 and won Pan American Games silver. Good athletic ability and physical edge, but career was disrupted by a two-year doping ban at 21.
inherited_summary: No evidence of family wealth or domain-specific advantages. Developed within Cuba's state sports system from age 12.
ecosystem_summary: Cuba's state sports system provided early training and national team access at 18. Career was disrupted by a doping ban (2006-2008), but he returned with Trentino Volley, an elite Italian club, winning multiple Champions League titles.

endowment_summary: Talented footballer but released from Lille's academy for academic and behavioral problems. Had to grind through lower-division French clubs, showing determination rather than early prodigy signs.
inherited_summary: Grew up in a low-income family in Boulogne-sur-Mer. Suffered severe facial scars from a car accident at age two. Father was a construction worker/chauffeur; family struggled financially.
ecosystem_summary: French football system provided academy access (Lille) but he was released and had to claw through lower divisions (Boulogne, Alès, Brest, Metz). No elite ecosystem access until breakthrough at Galatasaray and Marseille in mid-20s.

endowment_summary: Started skating at 7, competed at Olympics at 13, won European Championship bronze at 15, and dominated 1971-73 with three World titles and Olympic gold. Exceptional early trajectory in figure skating.
inherited_summary: Born to a working-class family in Bratislava. No family domain advantages; mother connected him to a local ice rink after watching European Championships on TV.
ecosystem_summary: Coach Hilda Múdra became his lifelong mentor from age 7, providing sustained individualized training. The Czechoslovak state sports system supported his career, and compulsory figures mastery was his domain specialty.

endowment_summary: Started handball relatively late at 14 after swimming, but progressed rapidly to CSKA Moscow's senior team by 17. Showed strong athleticism but not prodigy-level early achievement.
inherited_summary: Born in the Kirghiz SSR. No evidence of family wealth or domain-specific advantages in handball.
ecosystem_summary: Joined CSKA Moscow, one of the premier Soviet sports clubs, and progressed through the Soviet national team pipeline. Won IHF Junior World Championship in 1989, benefiting from the systematic Soviet sports infrastructure.

endowment_summary: Joined RK Partizan Bjelovar at 17 and entered the Yugoslav national team at 19. Solid, capable player but not a standout prodigy; benefited from team system.
inherited_summary: Born in Zagreb during WWII. No evidence of family wealth or domain-specific advantages.
ecosystem_summary: RK Partizan Bjelovar was his club for 15 years, and the Yugoslav national team system was a handball superpower. The team sport system provided elite competition and coaching at the international level.

endowment_summary: Charismatic and verbally skilled from young age, described as a 'good talker' and 'slick.' Began acting at 15 and self-released mixtapes from 2006. Not a musical prodigy but showed strong creative drive and networking ability.
inherited_summary: Parents divorced when he was 5; raised by single mother in modest circumstances. Father was a musician (drummer for Jerry Lee Lewis) but largely absent and incarcerated. Musical uncles Larry Graham (Sly and the Family Stone) and Teenie Hodges (Al Green) provided deep music lineage.
ecosystem_summary: Degrassi: The Next Generation provided a television platform and income from age 15. Lil Wayne's co-sign in 2009 was a career-changing endorsement. Toronto's emerging music scene and the internet mixtape era provided distribution timing.

endowment_summary: Pharmacy student at University of Geneva who won Olympic slalom gold as a surprise winner. Good skier but not a dominant force; her victory was unexpected, suggesting capable but not exceptional early ability.
inherited_summary: University-educated pharmacy student at Geneva, indicating a middle-class Swiss background with educational stability.
ecosystem_summary: Swiss national alpine skiing team provided training and competition access. Switzerland's winter sports tradition offered infrastructure, but she joined the national team only shortly before the Olympics.

endowment_summary: Co-founded manga club in high school and published first dōjinshi at 18. While not a childhood prodigy, her creative output intensified rapidly under professional training, and she serialized Urusei Yatsura by 21, demonstrating exceptional storytelling talent.
inherited_summary: Father Uki Takahashi was a doctor, haiku poet, and ink wash painter — an accomplished, middle-class family. Father was initially unsupportive of manga career but provided cultural and intellectual environment.
ecosystem_summary: Enrolled in Gekiga Sonjuku, Kazuo Koike's (Lone Wolf and Cub) manga school, which pushed students toward character-driven storytelling. Worked as assistant to horror manga artist Kazuo Umezu. Shogakukan's Weekly Shōnen Sunday provided a major publishing platform.

endowment_summary: Emerged as Norway's dominant speed skater starting at 21, winning Norwegian Allround Championships eight times. Strong long-distance specialist but not a childhood prodigy; worked as a carpenter during his competitive years.
inherited_summary: Born in Oslo, represented Aktiv SK. Working-class background; worked as a carpenter alongside his skating career. No family domain advantages.
ecosystem_summary: Norway's deep speed skating tradition and the Aktiv SK club provided elite training environment and competition. Norway was the global center of speed skating, offering world-class infrastructure and coaching.

endowment_summary: Started boxing at 8 and won Moroccan national senior championship at 19. Showed strong early commitment but competed at a regional level (Mediterranean Games gold) rather than global dominance in early years.
inherited_summary: Grew up in a working-class Casablanca neighborhood. Brother Mohamed was also a boxer, providing sibling domain exposure. No evidence of family wealth.
ecosystem_summary: Trained at Khachabate Al Hay Mohammadi boxing school under Mohamed Zarougui, introduced by local champion Mohamed Hajji. Moroccan national team pipeline provided competition access, but infrastructure was limited compared to global boxing powers.

endowment_summary: Won Girlfriend Model Search at 17 and was scouted at a beach. Natural 180cm height and distinctive look provided physical advantages. Not a prodigy but had strong physical attributes for modeling.
inherited_summary: Father Kim Kershaw played professional football (VFL for Richmond and Hawthorn) before becoming a financial adviser. Mother was a psychologist. Middle-class Melbourne family with professional sports background.
ecosystem_summary: Scouted by the same agent who discovered Miranda Kerr. Signed with Chic Management, then Next Management in New York. Fashion capital relocation to NYC provided industry access, but no exceptional mentor or institutional pipeline.

endowment_summary: Took up athletics at 17, relatively late, and joined the Soviet national team at 24. Won Estonian SSR titles at 19-21. Capable athlete but not a prodigy; his trajectory was steady rather than meteoric.
inherited_summary: Born into a sporting family in Tallinn; father Aadu Tarmak was the Soviet discus champion in 1943-44, providing direct domain knowledge and athletic lineage in the same sport system.
ecosystem_summary: Trained within the Soviet national team system and represented Dynamo Leningrad. The Soviet sports pipeline provided systematic coaching, facilities, and competition access at the highest level.

endowment_summary: Ajax's youngest-ever debutant at 16 years and 242 days, won Champions League at 19. Demonstrated exceptional early football ability with rapid professional trajectory and competitive maturity beyond his years.
inherited_summary: Born in Suriname, moved to Netherlands at 2. Father Johann was a former football player and talent agent. Footballing family with brothers Jürgen and Chedric also becoming professionals. Father's agent role provided direct industry connections.
ecosystem_summary: Recruited to Ajax's elite youth academy at 10 through Johan Cruyff's talent agency. Trained under Louis van Gaal with golden generation peers (de Boer twins, Davids, Kluivert). Ajax academy was one of the world's premier football development systems.

endowment_summary: Multilingual (five languages) and creatively gifted with sharp humor, but not a prodigy. Made film debut at 16 and started in TV at 20, showing early creative drive rather than exceptional early talent.
inherited_summary: Born into an affluent Brazilian family with diplomatic lineage — great-grandfather was a diplomat and provincial governor. Father was a businessman; family lived in Copacabana Palace annex. Studied at Swiss boarding school (Lycée Jaccard, Lausanne). Family business failed when he was a teenager.
ecosystem_summary: Rio de Janeiro was the center of Brazilian television during its boom years. Swiss education provided European cultural exposure. Early access to Rio's TV industry at the dawn of Brazilian television provided frontier-geography timing.

endowment_summary: Trained in multiple sports as a teenager before focusing on handball. Debuted at 16 and reached senior national team at 20. Exceptional physical attributes (194cm, 96kg, cannon arm) but not a prodigy in terms of early achievement.
inherited_summary: Born in Zalău, Romania. No evidence of family wealth or domain-specific advantages in handball.
ecosystem_summary: Romanian national team and Steaua București provided elite handball infrastructure. Romania was a world handball power in this era, with the national team winning World Championship gold in 1970.

endowment_summary: Developed an innovative modular housing thesis at McGill that became Habitat 67. Named University Scholar in his fifth year. Showed exceptional creative and architectural vision from his student years, though not a childhood prodigy.
inherited_summary: Father was a textile importer in Haifa from Aleppo; mother from Manchester. Middle-class family business provided stability until Israeli import restrictions hurt the business, forcing emigration to Montreal when Safdie was 15.
ecosystem_summary: McGill University architecture program, thesis advisor Sandy van Ginkel who connected him to Expo 67, apprenticeship with Louis Kahn in Philadelphia. Expo 67 was a once-in-a-generation platform that launched his career at 25. Montreal's World's Fair timing was perfect.

endowment_summary: Broke the World Hour Record for amateurs at 19, won the UCI Amateur Track World Championship at 20, and Olympic gold at 21. Exceptional early physical achievement in track cycling.
inherited_summary: Born in Arquata Scrivia, Italy in 1931. No evidence of family wealth or cycling-specific family background.
ecosystem_summary: Italy's deep cycling tradition and the amateur track cycling pipeline produced world-class riders in the post-war era. The Italian cycling system provided coaching, competition, and team pursuit infrastructure.

endowment_summary: Skating unaided at 3, up at 5 AM daily to skate on Lake Ontario as a child. Played junior B at 15 and was in the NHL at 18 without looking out of place. Exceptional raw physical talent recognized very early.
inherited_summary: Son of a cement company foreman in Point Anne, Ontario. Grew up on a farm near Belleville in a working-class family with eleven children. Father dreamed of playing pro hockey but needed steady income.
ecosystem_summary: Canadian hockey culture and the OHA junior pipeline (Woodstock Warriors, Galt Black Hawks, St. Catharines Teepees) provided elite development. Joined the Chicago Black Hawks at 18, a major NHL franchise.

endowment_summary: Began acting as a teenager in community theatre, made West End debut at 17. Capable actor with early start but not a prodigy; his trajectory was accelerated by elite institutional access rather than raw exceptional talent.
inherited_summary: Father was a Marks & Spencer executive and ex-Royal Artillery officer. Mother was a musician. Middle-class English family with cultural exposure but no direct theatre industry connections.
ecosystem_summary: National Youth Theatre as teenager, Oxford University Dramatic Society, and crucially, selection by Laurence Olivier for the National Theatre Company at 23. Franco Zeffirelli mentored and cast him. London's elite theatre ecosystem provided a once-in-a-generation platform.

endowment_summary: Learned chess at 4, won Sofia's women's championship at 7, world U10 champion at 10, debuted at Chess Olympiad at 13, Bulgarian women's champion at 16. Genuine prodigy-level ability with extraordinarily early specialization and dominance.
inherited_summary: Father Andon Stefanov, a designer/artist, taught her chess at 4 and was her only coach through her early career. Middle-class Sofia family with intellectual background but no professional chess lineage.
ecosystem_summary: Bulgaria's strong chess tradition provided a competitive environment. Father provided sustained individualized training from age 4. However, she noted she never had professional coaching until after winning European women's championship, suggesting limited institutional support early on.

endowment_summary: Karting at 10, German Junior Karting Champion at 15, German Kart Champion at 16. Systematic progression through every junior formula (Formula BMW, A1 GP, F3 Euro Series, GP2) winning championships at each level. Exceptional early racing trajectory.
inherited_summary: Father Klaus Dieter Hülkenberg owns a shipping company (Hülkenberg Spedition) in Emmerich. Upper-middle-class family with business resources that funded his racing career without financial constraints. Trained as freight forwarding agent at father's company.
ecosystem_summary: Spotted by Willi Weber, Michael Schumacher's long-time manager, who described him as 'unbelievable talent.' German motorsport boom of the Schumacher era created a fertile ecosystem. Weber's management opened doors in junior formulae.

endowment_summary: Started cross-country skiing at 11 and made World Cup debut at 18. Steady progression rather than prodigy-level dominance; first World Cup victory at 22, Olympic medals at 23.
inherited_summary: Born in Shchuchinsk, Kazakh SSR to Russian parents. No evidence of family wealth or skiing-specific family background.
ecosystem_summary: Trained within the Soviet Armed Forces sports society in Alma-Ata. The Soviet sports system provided systematic coaching, facilities, and competition access through a centralized pipeline.

endowment_summary: Started skiing at 4, joined jumping club at 10, World Cup debut at 17, first World Cup win at 18. Exceptional early trajectory with years of domain-specific practice before elite competition.
inherited_summary: Uncle connected him to the Ilirija Jumping Club at age 10, providing early domain access. No evidence of significant family wealth, but family connections facilitated sport entry.
ecosystem_summary: Grew up in Slovenia, home to Planica, one of the world's most famous ski flying venues, and a region with deep ski jumping culture. The Ilirija club and Slovenian ski jumping tradition provided elite training and infrastructure.

endowment_summary: Spotted as a natural running talent running barefoot at a railway competition. Joined Soviet national team at 18, won European relay gold at 21. Natural athletic ability but not prodigy-level in terms of structured early achievement.
inherited_summary: Grew up in a working-class family in Kotelnich. Poverty evident from running barefoot at competitions. No family domain advantages.
ecosystem_summary: Coach Valentina Dorogova spotted her and guided her into the Soviet athletics pipeline. The Lokomotiv club and Soviet national team provided systematic training, facilities, and competition access.

endowment_summary: Senior Wrangler at Cambridge (top mathematics student), Tyson Medal for astrophysics, Smith's Prize, completed PhD under Fred Hoyle at 25, co-developed Hoyle-Narlikar theory of gravitation. Prodigious mathematical and theoretical physics ability from school age.
inherited_summary: Father Vishnu Vasudev Narlikar was a mathematics professor and general relativity pioneer at BHU. Mother was a Sanskrit scholar. Maternal uncle V. S. Huzurbazar was a statistician. Exceptional academic family providing direct domain knowledge and intellectual environment.
ecosystem_summary: Grew up on BHU campus with academic visitors. Cambridge University (Fitzwilliam College, like his father), Fred Hoyle as PhD advisor. Contemporaries included Stephen Hawking. The Cambridge mathematical tripos and Hoyle's supervision represented a once-in-a-generation intellectual environment.

endowment_summary: Started formal badminton training at 11, won Surabaya junior championship at 12, national junior championship at 15, and All England (badminton's most prestigious title) at 18. Exceptional early trajectory in a highly competitive sport.
inherited_summary: Father Zulkarnain Kurniawan set up a badminton club in a railway station warehouse and coached him intensively from age 11. Family owned tailoring and dairy businesses providing financial stability. Sister Utami Dewi was a five-time national badminton champion.
ecosystem_summary: Indonesia was a global badminton powerhouse. Father's club, then Rajawali Club with many elite players, and the National Training Center from age 16 provided progressive elite training environments. Indonesian badminton culture and infrastructure were world-leading.

endowment_summary: Started gymnastics in hometown and progressed through Soviet sports boarding school. World all-around champion at 20, Olympic team gold at 21. Strong gymnast developed through the system rather than a prodigy.
inherited_summary: Born to a working-class family in Oleksandriya, Ukrainian SSR. No family domain advantages; entered the Soviet gymnastics pipeline when a coach spotted him at school.
ecosystem_summary: Transferred to a sports boarding school in Lugansk for intensive specialized training. The Soviet gymnastics system was world-dominant, providing elite coaching, facilities, and the national team pipeline from age 19.

endowment_summary: Taught himself piano and guitar as a teen, formed vocal trio, recorded first single at 14, and wrote 'Diana' at 16 which sold 20 million copies. Exceptional early musical and songwriting ability with massive commercial success as a teenager.
inherited_summary: Lebanese Christian immigrant parents in Ottawa owned a restaurant (the Locanda) popular with local entertainers, providing early exposure to performance world. Middle-class immigrant family; father was civically engaged. Mother died when he was 18.
ecosystem_summary: Ottawa restaurant environment provided entertainment industry exposure. Uncle gave $100 for his first NYC trip at 16. ABC-Paramount record deal provided distribution. The rock and roll wave of the late 1950s created perfect timing for a teen idol.

endowment_summary: Started golf at 12, joined Swedish national team at 16, won NCAA individual championship at University of Arizona, world amateur champion, and LPGA Player of the Year at 24. Exceptional multi-sport athlete who rapidly excelled in golf.
inherited_summary: Father Tom was an IBM executive; mother Gunilla worked in a bank. Upper-middle-class Swedish family with strong sporting culture. Both parents were avid golfers; younger sister Charlotta also became an LPGA Tour winner.
ecosystem_summary: Swedish national team pipeline and developing golf infrastructure provided elite training. University of Arizona NCAA golf program offered college-level competition and coaching. Family moved to London for father's work, exposing her to international golf culture.

endowment_summary: Capable military officer who rose through ranks and befriended Gaddafi during military college. Showed leadership and organizational ability but no evidence of exceptional cognitive or creative endowment.
inherited_summary: Member of the Obeidat tribe, one of Libya's most powerful and respected tribes. Tribal affiliation provided social standing and networks within Libyan society, though not wealth-based advantage.
ecosystem_summary: Military college provided the platform to build a close friendship with Gaddafi. The 1969 Libyan revolution created perfect timing for a young officer to ascend to power. Gaddafi's inner circle provided direct access to state power.

endowment_summary: Published first comic strip at 16 in Vers l'Avenir. Prolific from a young age, creating multiple series and working across genres by his mid-20s. Exceptional early creative output and storytelling ability in comics.
inherited_summary: Born Michel Régnier in Ixelles, Belgium in 1931, grew up in Herstal near Liège. No evidence of family wealth or comics-specific family background.
ecosystem_summary: Belgium was the epicenter of Franco-Belgian comics. Worked alongside André Franquin at Spirou magazine, who mentored him and improved his craft. The Spirou magazine ecosystem and Franco-Belgian comics industry provided a world-class creative environment.

endowment_summary: Started gymnastics at 9 on teacher's recommendation, became junior national all-around champion at 16, won first World Championship medal at 18. Exceptional early gymnastic achievement, particularly on pommel horse.
inherited_summary: Father Ivan was a navy officer, mother Pavla was a housekeeper and seamstress. Working-class family with no gymnastics domain background. Father was absent during wartime; raised partly by grandparents.
ecosystem_summary: TVD Partizan Narodni dom, the first Slovene gymnastics club (est. 1863), provided training from age 9. Yugoslav national team system provided elite competition access. His rapid development was noted due to excellent physical preparation.

endowment_summary: Achieved 8 A-levels and 13 O-levels at Brentwood School (though failed History). Exceptional academic capacity and language skills; leveraged German fluency and archival research abilities to write bestselling first book at 25.
inherited_summary: Father was a Royal Navy commander and prolific maritime author. Mother was a professional illustrator and writer (BBC, Radio Times). Literary household with domain overlap in writing and research, though parents separated and family lived in straitened circumstances.
ecosystem_summary: Brentwood School provided solid education. Imperial College and UCL provided university access. Working in Germany as a steelworker gave him German language skills and archival access. The WWII history wave of the 1960s provided market timing for his first book.

endowment_summary: Started racing at 16, won Venezuelan national championship at 17, became youngest motorcycle road racing world champion at 19. Exceptional early racing talent with rapid rise to world championship level.
inherited_summary: Father Giovanni was a former Venezuelan national motorcycle racing champion and motorcycle shop owner. Italian immigrant family with direct domain access — motorcycles, equipment, racing knowledge, and professional network from birth.
ecosystem_summary: Father's motorcycle shop provided equipment and mechanical knowledge. Venezuelan Yamaha importer provided sponsorship and factory-level machinery. The post-war motorcycle racing boom and access to ex-works Yamaha bikes through importer connections provided elite competition access.

endowment_summary: Started playing handball as a child at Grótta. Despite small stature (1.8m, 68kg as a young player), developed into an elite left wing through coaching and determination. Good but not prodigy-level early ability.
inherited_summary: Parents were not sporty; no handball family background. Great-grandfather was a water polo player and international football referee, but no direct domain advantage for handball.
ecosystem_summary: Iceland's unique handball culture gives youngsters early senior team opportunities — he played senior team handball at 16. Coach Gauti Gretason at Grótta discovered and developed his talent. Icelandic handball system provided a distinctive developmental pathway.

endowment_summary: Introduced to chess at 6 by older brother, earned Grandmaster title at 18, won Asian Championship at 19. Demonstrated exceptional chess depth through obsessive self-study, studying chess books secretly at night under the covers.
inherited_summary: Lost his father young and grew up amid post-Soviet economic turmoil in Uzbekistan. No family wealth or chess-specific background; brother provided initial introduction to the game.
ecosystem_summary: Soviet chess tradition in Tashkent provided foundational training through a local sports academy. The Soviet chess school's emphasis on rigorous endgame and tactical study shaped his development despite post-Soviet economic disruption.

endowment_summary: Began artistic practice at 18, created first Dé-coll/age at 22, staged one of the first Happenings in European art history at 25. Innovative and pioneering but not a childhood prodigy; his talent emerged through post-war artistic exploration.
inherited_summary: Father was a railway worker in Leverkusen. Working-class family in post-war Germany. Evacuated to Sudetenland during WWII, returned to Leverkusen in 1945. No family wealth or artistic background.
ecosystem_summary: Studied at prestigious art schools: École Nationale Supérieur des Beaux Arts in Paris (1955-56) and Düsseldorf Academy of Arts (1957). Post-war European avant-garde movement and Fluxus network provided a frontier creative environment.

endowment_summary: Started fencing after growing up near the Kamuti fencing brothers. Won youth team championship at 19 and Olympic team épée gold at 25. Capable fencer developed through Hungary's elite system rather than prodigy-level early talent.
inherited_summary: Grew up in the same building as the Kamuti fencing brothers who inspired his sport choice. Father died when he was young; coach Dr. Bay Béla served as a father figure. No family wealth or direct domain advantages.
ecosystem_summary: Hungary's elite fencing tradition and the BVSC Budapest club, one of the country's top fencing centers, provided world-class coaching. Coaches Hatz József, Vári Attila, and Dr. Bay Béla provided sustained mentorship within a globally dominant fencing system.

endowment_summary: Started competing internationally at 21, did not win medals until 23, and broke through at 24 with World and European Allround titles. Late bloomer with steady but not exceptional early trajectory.
inherited_summary: Born in Alanäset, Jämtland, Sweden, a small town with no documented family advantages in sport. No evidence of family wealth or domain-specific background.
ecosystem_summary: Sweden's winter sports tradition and the IF Castor club in Östersund provided training infrastructure. Swedish speed skating culture offered competition access, but Ericsson's international career started relatively late at 21.

endowment_summary: IMO gold medals 1964-1966 with perfect scores in 1965 and 1966. Published first research paper at 17. Awarded C.Sc. by Hungarian Academy of Sciences at 22 with 15 published papers. Prodigious mathematical ability from early adolescence, mentored by Paul Erdős at 14.
inherited_summary: Father was a surgeon; family lived in relative comfort in Budapest. No mathematicians in the family, but middle-class professional background provided stability and educational support. Father hoped he would pursue medicine.
ecosystem_summary: Attended Fazekas Mihály Gimnázium's specialized math class — a once-in-a-generation peer environment with future mathematicians including his wife Katalin Vesztergombi. Paul Erdős as mentor from age 14. Budapest's unique mathematics education culture and Hungarian combinatorial school were world-leading.

endowment_summary: Professional gymnast for over 10 years, Czech national team member for 5 years, national champion 4 times. Strong athletic foundation and physical conditioning, but not prodigy-level; transitioned to modeling at 19.
inherited_summary: Born in Brno, Czechoslovakia. No evidence of family wealth or domain-specific advantages. Brother was a fireman; no athletic family background documented.
ecosystem_summary: Czech national gymnastics system provided elite training and competition access. Discovered by a scout while running, leading to modeling career. Penthouse platform provided industry visibility, but no exceptional mentor or institutional pipeline for modeling.
